narrative.overview:
The UI is one manager's own instrument, read on a phone before kickoff or a laptop midweek, and it is set like a broadcast lineup graphic: a near-black field, one panel per player cut out on his club's colours, the projection in big condensed numerals, and the verdict in a squared lower-third chip. The call reads from across the room; the paragraph is there when he wants it.

The world is established on the Roster page (`web/app/roster`, `web/components/roster-cards.tsx`, `player-media.tsx`, `outlook.tsx`) as of 2026-09-08, and extended the same day to the navigation (`nav.tsx`, `nav-links.tsx`) and the Matchup page (`web/app/page.tsx`, `matchup.tsx`), then on 2026-09-09 to the League page (`web/app/league`, `league.tsx`, `club-logo.tsx`, `week-select.tsx`) and the Waivers page (`web/app/waivers`, `waiver-table.tsx`, `pos-tabs.tsx`), and on 2026-09-13 to the play feed (`play-feed.tsx`, `web/app/plays`). Journal and Draft still carry the stock shadcn neutral look (Geist `text-xl` titles, default pills, muted-footer cards, tables). They have not been brought over yet; the Roster page is the reference when they are. This file records the board, not the leftover.

Everything is a shadcn (base-ui) component. New looks are expressed by extending a shadcn variant (`badge.tsx` adds the verdict colours and a `shape: chip` axis) or by laying a shadcn Card out with grid utilities, never by hand-rolling an element. Tailwind 4, Next 16, lucide icons. Dark follows the system; there is no toggle, and `.light`/`.dark` classes exist only as hooks.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black field in dark, off-white press-box light in light; both are the same board.
Team-colour gradient panels from the 32-club table are the only saturated surfaces besides the three verdict colours.
Barlow Condensed for names, numerals and labels; Geist for reasons and prose; Geist Mono for slot codes in tables.
Three verdict colours (lime START, amber close/questionable, red OUT/IR); nothing else is coloured.
One card shadow, one authored motion (the outlook panel opening), no decoration beyond the watermark.

rules.name: The Three Verdicts Rule
rules.body: Lime, amber and red mean START, close/questionable and OUT/IR, and nothing else. No other hue is added for state; blue, green or purple accents do not exist here.

rules.name: The Club Owns the Colour Rule
rules.body: Saturation on the board comes from the team table, never from the design tokens. Text is never set on a club colour.

rules.name: The Condensed-for-Facts Rule
rules.body: Names, numbers, units and verdict labels are Barlow Condensed; sentences are Geist. A number set in Geist or a sentence set in Barlow is off-system.

rules.name: The Unit Beside the Number Rule
rules.body: A big numeral always carries its small uppercase unit (PROJ or PTS) on its baseline; the number never stands alone.

rules.name: The Decision Above the Fold Rule
rules.body: On a phone the card shows name, matchup, projection, chip and reason before anything that does not change the call; prose is behind a tap.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: The card drop is the only box shadow on a surface. Chips, buttons, tables and headings are flat.

dos: Do express a new look as a shadcn variant (as `badge.tsx` does with `start/close/warn/out/muted` and `shape: chip`) and lay shadcn Cards out with grid utilities; the component library is the only element vocabulary.
Do set names, numerals, units and chip labels in Barlow Condensed with `tabular-nums`, and sentences in Geist.
Do put the club's colour in the panel from `web/lib/teams.ts` and load marks and portraits from ESPN's CDN with the logo-then-nothing fallback; never a broken-image glyph.
Do keep the stale badge and the "facts changed since" stamp; stale is a state, and every surface says when it was last true.
Do bring a page onto the board by reusing the Roster page's tokens and chips (a Matchup row is a smaller card, not a new colour scheme).
donts: Don't add a fourth state colour or use lime, amber or red for anything but START, close/questionable and OUT/IR.
Don't set text on a team-colour panel.
Don't stack shadows, add hover lifts, or put a shadow on a chip or button; the card drop is the only one.
Don't use the pill badge for a verdict on a board surface; verdicts are squared chips.
Don't add a theme toggle or a theme provider; dark follows `prefers-color-scheme`.
Don't hand-roll a div-and-span element when a shadcn primitive exists.
